content: No, that is not true. Romansh is one of Switzerland's four official languages, alongside German, French, and Italian. However, its use is limited primarily to the Romansh-speaking region in the canton of Graubünden (Grisons). While Romansh is recognized as an official language at the federal level, its application to all official documents and for all federal authorities is not as extensive as the other three languages. It is used in official contexts within its traditional region but does not have the same universal applicability across all federal communications and documentation as the other official languages.
